symptoms: Not a recognizable plant or crop leaf.
causes: Camera pointed at a non-plant object.
prevention: Ensure the crop leaf is clearly visible and well-lit.

symptoms: Small, yellow-green spots on young leaves.
Spots turn brown or black with a yellow halo.
Severely affected leaves may drop prematurely.
organicTreatment: Remove and destroy infected plant parts.
chemicalTreatment: Copper hydroxide or copper sulfate sprays.
prevention: Ensure adequate plant spacing for airflow.

symptoms: Vibrant green leaves.
No visible spots or discoloration.
Firm stems and healthy growth.
prevention: Continue current watering and fertilizing practices.

symptoms: Brown or black spots on older leaves.
Spots often have concentric rings (target-board appearance).
Yellowing of surrounding tissue.
causes: Warm, humid weather and stressed plants.
prevention: Crop rotation (do not plant tomatoes or potatoes in same spot).

symptoms: Irregular, water-soaked spots on leaves.
White fungal growth on the undersides of leaves in humid conditions.
Tubers develop brown, necrotic lesions.
causes: Cool, wet, and highly humid weather.
organicTreatment: Prompt removal and destruction of infected plants.
chemicalTreatment: Fungicides containing metalaxyl, chlorothalonil, or cymoxanil.
prevention: Destroy volunteer potatoes and cull piles.

symptoms: Leaves are uniformly green.
Vigorous plant growth without lesions.
causes: Optimal environment and good soil health.

symptoms: Small, water-soaked, greasy spots on leaves.
Spots turn black with a yellow halo.
Fruit may develop scab-like spots.
organicTreatment: Prune infected leaves using sterilized tools.
prevention: Rotate crops away from solanaceous plants.

symptoms: Dark, target-like spots with concentric rings on lower leaves.
Lower leaves turn yellow and drop.
Stem lesions may appear.
prevention: Stake or cage plants to keep foliage off the ground.

symptoms: Large, dark, water-soaked blotches on leaves and stems.
White mold on the underside of leaves.
Firm, dark brown lesions on fruit.
Pale greenish-yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces.
Olive-green to brown velvety mold on lower leaf surfaces.
Leaves wither and drop.
causes: High relative humidity (above 85%) and poor airflow.
organicTreatment: Neem oil or potassium bicarbonate sprays.
prevention: Maximize airflow through pruning and wide spacing.
Water at the base of the plant.

symptoms: Numerous small, circular spots with dark borders and gray centers.
Tiny black fruiting bodies in the center of spots.
Lower leaves turn yellow, wither, and fall.
prevention: Remove lower leaves near the soil.
Apply mulch to prevent soil splashing.

symptoms: Leaves appear stippled, pale, or yellow.
Fine, silky webbing on the undersides of leaves.
Leaves may eventually turn brown and drop.
organicTreatment: Strong water spray to dislodge mites.
prevention: Keep plants well-watered (mites thrive in dry conditions).
Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural predators.

symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on leaves.
Pitted, brown spots on fruit.
Defoliation starting from the bottom.
prevention: Remove crop debris at the end of the season.

symptoms: Severe stunting of the plant.
Leaves cup upward, turning yellow between veins.
Reduced fruit setting.
causes: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV), transmitted by whiteflies.
organicTreatment: Control whiteflies using neem oil or insecticidal soap.

symptoms: Mottled light and dark green areas on leaves (mosaic pattern).
Stunted growth and distorted leaves.
Internal browning of fruit.
causes: Tobacco mosaic virus (TMV) or Tomato mosaic virus (ToMV).
Mechanically transmitted via hands, tools, or contaminated seeds.
organicTreatment: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately.
Wash hands and sterilize tools with milk or bleach.
chemicalTreatment: None available. Prevention is the only method.
prevention: Do not use tobacco products near plants.

symptoms: Green, vigorous foliage.
Even growth without spotting or discoloration.
Firm, blemish-free fruit development.
